questions.prompt: Which failure is most likely to fix itself if you wait and retry with backoff?

options.text: A 503 meaning the model is temporarily overloaded
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says to follow Retry-After when present, then retry.

options.text: A 400 meaning one input in the request is not valid
options.explanation: A 400 points to a problem with the request. Google and Runway say not to retry it.

options.text: A task rejected with a SAFETY.INPUT failure code
options.explanation: Runway says you should not retry these.

questions.prompt: Why add jitter to the wait between retries?

options.text: So the vendor treats the retry as a brand new request
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs says jitter changes how a request is treated.

options.text: So clients do not all retry at the same moment
options.explanation: Right. Runway and Google both describe jitter as a small random delay for this reason.

options.text: So the retry costs less than the first request
options.explanation: Jitter changes timing only. It does not change the price.

questions.prompt: A 429 says your organization has no credits left. What next?

options.text: Retry with growing pauses until it finally works
options.explanation: Pauses help with a temporary rate limit. They do not add credits.

options.text: Add credits or change the limit, then retry
options.explanation: Right. Retrying billing, spend or quota errors does not restore access.
